newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, U.S. sign bilateral copyright treaty.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, U.S. sign bilateral copyright treaty.

text.p: Vietnam and the United States have signed a bilateral copyright treaty, officials at the U.S. embassy in Hanoi said on Thursday.

They said the agreement would mean that U.S. copyright owners will enjoy legal protection against piracy in Vietnam for the first time, while Vietnamese authors and producers will have similar protection in the United States.

The International Intellectual Property Alliance (IIPA) welcomed the treaty on behalf of U.S. copyright industries, saying it meant Vietnam would have to bring its copyright laws and enforcement practices closer to world standards and treat U.S. and local copyright owners equally.

IIPA said in a statement that piracy of copyright materials such as movies and software in Vietnam was inflicting over $50 million in trade losses anually and threatening the potential for U.S. exports to one of the world's fastest growing markets.
Joseph Damond, chief negotiator from a U.S. trade mission in Hanoi this week, said on Wednesday that implementation and enforcement details of the treaty still must be established.
Hanoi and Washington normalised diplomatic ties in 1995, but progress towards a full trade agreement has so far been slow.
Damond described the copyright deal as "a good start" in that process, but gave no date for likely full economic normalisation.
